executive_summary: The Docker environment hosting the ICS lab has critical vulnerabilities in the grfics-router image, exposing the network to potential exploitation. Containers on the ICS network (PLC, EWS, simulation) and DMZ (router, Caldera) lack resource limits and have published ports, increasing risk. Immediate remediation is required to prevent OT process disruption and data compromise.

findings.title: Critical Vulnerabilities in grfics-router Image
findings.explanation: The router image contains critical vulnerabilities in base packages (perl-base, zlib1g, libsqlite3-0) that could allow remote code execution or privilege escalation. Since the router is exposed on the DMZ (port 51820/udp), this directly threatens network segmentation and ICS integrity.
findings.remediation: Update the grfics-router image to versions with fixes (e.g., perl-base 5.36.0-7+deb12u4) and re-scan with Trivy to confirm resolution.

rejected.title: ICS Network Containers Lack Resource Limits
rejected.explanation: Containers on the ICS network (PLC, EWS, simulation) lack memory and CPU limits, risking resource exhaustion that could disrupt OT processes or allow DoS attacks.
rejected.remediation: Add resource limits in Docker Compose or docker run commands for all ICS network containers (e.g., --memory=512m --cpus=1).

rejected.title: Published Ports on ICS Network Containers
rejected.explanation: The HMI container exposes a web interface (port 6081) on the ICS network, creating a direct attack vector for OT process manipulation if the service is vulnerable.
rejected.remediation: Remove the published port or restrict it to internal network IPs only (e.g., --publish 192.168.95.1:6081->8080/tcp).

recommendations: Immediately update grfics-router to versions with fixes for CVE-2026-13221 and other critical vulnerabilities.
Apply resource limits to all ICS network containers using Docker Compose or run commands.
Restrict published ports on ICS network containers to internal IPs only.
Scan all other ICS-related images (grfics-plc, grfics-workstation) with Trivy for vulnerabilities.
Implement network segmentation rules to prevent DMZ containers from accessing ICS network resources directly.
